title: In the countryside
description: Name the things outside the town, and say where they are.
grammar: gender and articles, and prepositions of place
grammarNote: The country has its own nouns, and estar says where each of them is.

explanation.summary: Outside the town the vocabulary opens up: fields, rivers, hills and animals. The grammar is the one you already know.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El campo, el bosque, el río, el monte, el caballo y la abeja are masculine. La granja, la piedra y la oveja are feminine. El campo is the countryside and the field at the same time, and el monte is a hill or a mountain.

sections.heading: Where they are
sections.body: Estar says where a thing is, and outside the town you use it with big places: el caballo está en el campo, la granja está cerca del río. En el campo and en la granja are the two you will use most.

examples.es: la abeja está en la flor
examples.en: the bee is on the flower

examples.es: el caballo está en el campo
examples.en: the horse is in the field

examples.es: hay una piedra en el camino
examples.en: there is a stone on the path

items.note: Masculine: el campo. It also means the field.
Masculine: el río. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el monte. It can also mean a mountain.
Feminine: la oveja. The plural is las ovejas.

drills.meaning: the sheep are in the field
the farm is near the river
the horse has a big wheel
